title: Tenali and the Leaking Temple Idol

full_text:
At a prominent temple near the palace, a haughty and avaricious chief priest named Somayaji hoarded all the food offerings brought by devotees. While poor beggars starved outside the temple gates, Somayaji and his relatives feasted on mounds of ghee rice, sweet laddus, and milk puddings, throwing the surplus to stray dogs rather than sharing a single grain with the needy.

He claimed: 'The deity consumes the spiritual essence, and the sacred leftovers belong exclusively to my family by divine right!'

Tenali Raman resolved to correct this injustice.
He hired a master sculptor to craft an exact replica of the temple's stone pedestal. Inside the stone base, the sculptor carved a hidden channel leading through a small copper pipe straight out the temple foundation into an open stone trough outside the courtyard wall, where the poor sat.

Tenali then donated a magnificent, large bronze vessel to the temple, placing it before the altar directly over the concealed drain.

The next morning, when devotees poured hundreds of pots of sweet milk, honey, and clarified butter over the altar, the liquids flowed into the bronze vessel and immediately drained through the concealed channel straight into the stone trough outside!
The hungry beggars and orphans outside the wall joyfully filled their clay cups with fresh milk and honey, drinking to their hearts' content!

Inside, Somayaji stood with his empty copper pots, staring in utter bewilderment:
'Heavens! Where has all the milk gone? The altar is completely dry!'

Tenali, who was standing among the worshippers, proclaimed loudly:
'Rejoice, citizens of Vijayanagara! For forty years, the priest claimed the deity only ate spiritual essence. But today, the deity has grown so compassionate that it has drunk all the milk physically, and miraculously poured it straight into the mouths of the hungry children outside!'

The entire crowd ran outside and saw the happy children drinking. They cheered and praised the miracle!
When Somayaji inspected the altar and discovered the hidden pipe, he angrily confronted Tenali.
Tenali looked at him with unwavering moral clarity:
'Somayaji, the true altar of the divine is the hungry stomach of an innocent child. If your prayers cannot teach you to feed the poor, a hollow stone pipe will do the work for you!'

Ashamed before the entire city and fearing the King's censure, the priest reformed his ways, instituting a daily communal kitchen for the poor that distributed temple food freely to all in need.
moral: Hypocrisy that hoards offerings meant for the divine while neglecting the starving poor is exposed by righteous ingenuity.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Greedy Priest"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
